request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]

Age: 82

Sex: Female

Reason for Hospitalization:
The patient presented to the emergency department with epigastric pain, heartburn, and nausea due to a large hiatus hernia with a portion of the stomach within the intrathoracic cavity.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the Observation department and was treated with nasogastric decompression, zero diet, fluid therapy, a prokinetic and a proton pump inhibitor, which resulted in clinical improvement. The patient was then discharged and advised to perform an upper endoscopy, but declined due to her age and multiple comorbidities.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient received nasogastric decompression, zero diet, fluid therapy, a prokinetic and a proton pump inhibitor, which resulted in clinical improvement. The patient was advised to perform an upper endoscopy, but declined surgical intervention or any other invasive intervention.

Follow-up:
The patient was advised to continue with dietary advice and pharmacological treatment directed at her symptoms. A solid link with the family doctor was made, leading to the optimal possible resolution of the patient's symptoms and improved physical and mental well-being.

Disposition:
The patient was discharged with outpatient follow-up.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the episode is a large hiatus hernia with part of the stomach in the intrathoracic cavity, which caused the epigastric pain, heartburn and nausea. In ICD-10-AM this falls under K44, Diaphragmatic hernia, in Chapter XI (Diseases of the digestive system).

The symptoms are integral to the hernia, so they are not coded as the principal diagnosis. The summary does not mention obstruction, gangrene or reflux oesophagitis, so K44 (hernia without obstruction or gangrene) is the appropriate category.

CODE: K44
